items.q: Why is the guild so strict about reporting?

a.v: Bookkeeping is required by law in Sweden. The Accounting Act applies to everyone running a business activity, and D-sektionen is one, so we have to comply with it.

The act contains the guidelines and requirements the Swedish Tax Agency places on us as an organisation. Breaking it can have serious consequences both for the guild and for the treasurer as a private person. The rules on this page are not here to make life difficult. They are here to keep us on the right side of the law.

items.q: Who does this apply to?

a.v: Everyone who buys something on behalf of the guild. If you hold a post, you will almost certainly need to make an expense claim for D-sektionen at some point during the year.
If you chair a committee, approval applies to you as well: you review and approve the expenses belonging to your committee before they are booked.

items.q: What is an expense claim?

a.v: An expense claim covers a cost you pay on someone else's behalf. You spend your own money on something the guild is going to pay for, and you are reimbursed afterwards.

items.q: Do I always get my money back?

a.v: No, reimbursement is not automatic. You are entitled to it when both of these are true:

v: Your committee chair approved the purchase.
You can support the purchase with a valid receipt.

a.v: ALWAYS check with your committee chair before making a purchase. If the requirements are not met, you risk having to pay for it yourself.

items.q: What should I do before I buy anything?

v: Clear the purchase with your committee chair and get an approval.
Make sure you get a valid receipt at the register, not just an order confirmation or a card slip.
Report the purchase here on the site as soon as you get home.

items.q: Who gets a guild card?

a.v: If your post involves many or expensive purchases, you get a guild card. It is tied to D-sektionen's bank account, so you don't have to spend your own money up front.

items.q: Can I buy whatever I want with the guild card?

a.v: No. A guild card does NOT mean you may buy whatever you like. Every purchase on a guild card must be approved by your committee chair in advance, and every purchase must be reported afterwards.
If unauthorised purchases are made on your guild card, you become personally liable for them.

items.q: My card was declined at the register, what do I do?

a.v: That means we haven't moved enough money over to the card account. If it is urgent, your best move is to call us straight away:

items.q: Can I lend out my guild card?

a.v: No. A guild card must never be lent to anyone else. It belongs to you and to your post.

items.q: Can I put a purchase on an invoice?

a.v: Yes, if you are offered the option of paying by invoice you may take it.
ALWAYS check with your committee chair before putting anything on an invoice. If the requirements are not met, you risk having to pay for it yourself.

items.q: Who should the invoice be addressed to?

a.v: The guild. Make sure the supplier invoices D-sektionen and not you as a private person.
The guild will NEVER pay invoices that are not addressed to the guild. If you have been invoiced privately, you have to pay the invoice yourself and then file it as an expense claim.

items.q: How do I report a purchase?

a.v: Every purchase must be reported. That is what entitles you to reimbursement for a private expense, and what keeps you from becoming personally liable for a guild card purchase. When you report, you fill in:

v: An overall title describing the transaction.
Whether the purchase was made with a guild card or privately.
Cost centre and amount for each part of the purchase.

a.v: Report a purchase

items.q: Can I put several receipts on one report?

a.v: Yes, if the receipts concern THE SAME EVENT, for instance two separate purchases on the same day for the same event. Press "add receipt" and report them together.
Receipts belonging to different events must be reported separately.

items.q: The receipt has to hit several cost centres, how do I split it?

a.v: Add one row per cost centre and report the costs separately there, with a comment explaining what the row covers. The rows must add up to the total on the receipt.

items.q: How do I report alcohol?

a.v: Alcohol comes with additional laws to comply with. One of the requirements is that alcoholic drinks and alcohol-like preparations must be reported separately by category:

v: Wine: up to 22 ‰, port, sherry, vermouth.
Other fermented drinks: cider, fruit wines, mead.

a.v: In practice that means splitting the alcohol you bought across one row per category: add up everything in the same category and put it on its own row, deposit (pant) included.
If you are unsure which category a drink belongs to, always ask your committee chair. The most common mistake is filing spirits as another fermented drink: Halmstad Crush is a spirit, not a cider.

items.q: Example: how do I split a Systembolaget purchase?

a.v: Say you bought the following for a sittning:

v: Pistonhead Haze Lager (beer): 2 × 11.90 kr + 2 × 1 kr deposit.
Briska Fläder (other fermented drink): 16.90 kr + 1 kr deposit.

items.q: How quickly do I have to report?

a.v: Under the financial policy, the treasurer has the right to hold you personally liable if a purchase (a private expense as well as a guild card purchase) is not reported within 60 days of the purchase being made.
The treasury does not have time to chase you to report on time. Report your purchases immediately.

items.q: I returned an item, does that have to be reported?

a.v: Yes. Returns of goods intended for the guild are reported exactly like purchases, except that the amount you enter must be negative.

items.q: I'm buying from abroad, is there anything special to keep in mind?

a.v: Pay through Klarna if you can. Other countries are not bound by Swedish rules and are therefore not obliged to give you a receipt the way a Swedish seller is. But if the purchase goes through Klarna, Klarna always gives you a valid receipt.

items.q: What counts as a valid receipt?

a.v: Under the Accounting Act (chapter 5, section 7), the verification must state when it was compiled, when the transaction took place, what it concerns, the amount, the counterparty, and a verification number or other identification.

If any of the above is missing, or cannot be made out CLEARLY, the approval will be rejected. You then have to request a valid receipt from the supplier.

items.q: Is an order confirmation enough?

a.v: No. An order confirmation is by default not a receipt. Ask the seller for a proper one.

items.q: Till receipt from a shop

a.v: Date, every item with its price, the VAT rates, the seller's company name, address and organisation number, and a receipt number, all present and all legible.

a.alt: Till receipt showing the date, items, VAT and the seller's organisation number.

items.q: Receipt from an online shop

a.v: A real receipt, or an invoice addressed to the guild, carrying the same details as a till receipt. The email you got when you placed the order is not this.

a.alt: Online shop receipt with seller details, VAT and a verification number.

items.q: Order confirmation

a.v: Confirms that an order was placed, not that it was paid. It carries no verification number and rarely states VAT. Ask for a receipt once the goods ship.

a.alt: Order confirmation from an online shop, without a verification number or VAT.

items.q: Receipt without seller details

a.v: Without the seller's company name, address and organisation number the counterparty cannot be established, and the receipt does not work as a verification.

a.alt: Receipt missing the seller's name, address and organisation number.

items.q: Receipt without VAT

a.v: The tax rates have to be visible. Documentation showing only the total cannot be booked. The card terminal slip is the most common example.

a.alt: Card terminal slip showing only the total amount.

items.q: Blurry or cropped photo

a.v: If the text cannot be made out CLEARLY, or part of the receipt is outside the frame, the approval is rejected. Shoot straight down, in good light, with the whole receipt in view.

a.alt: Blurry photo of a receipt with the bottom edge cut off.

items.q: What does approving an expense mean?

a.v: Approving means reviewing and signing off a transaction before it is booked. If you chair a committee, you approve the expenses belonging to it.
Go to approvals

items.q: What should I check before I approve?

a.v: The documentation has to be satisfactory. Ask yourself these questions before signing off a transaction:

v: Does the stated date match the date on the receipt?
Is the description appropriate for the goods?
Is guild card versus private card stated correctly?
